sources.entry: Pinepods - Podcast management system with multi-user support. Pinepods utilizes a central database so aspects like listen time and themes follow from device to device. (Demo, Source Code) GPL-3.0 Docker

summary.one_liner: PinePods is a self-hosted, multi-user podcast management system written in Rust that keeps subscriptions, listening history, queue, and settings in one central database so they sync across devices.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes a single server that a household connects to through a web client, native desktop and mobile apps, and a terminal CLI called Firewood. Data is stored in PostgreSQL or MySQL/MariaDB, with Valkey or Redis required as a cache. It supports audio and video podcasts with variable speed, chapters, transcripts, downloads, a persistent queue, serial auto-play, and per-podcast auto-download. Organization features include smart and manual playlists, saved episodes, favorites, full history, and local file-system podcasts. Discovery searches Podcast Index, iTunes, and YouTube, plus episode search within your own library and podcast-host following via PodPeople DB. It also includes a built-in gpodder-compatible sync server for apps like AntennaPod, OIDC/SSO, MFA/TOTP, OPML import/export, and push notifications through ntfy or webhooks.
use_cases: self-host a podcast player for a family
sync podcast listening progress across devices
keep using AntennaPod with a self-hosted backend
manage podcast subscriptions and downloads on a home server
listen to podcasts from the terminal
how_to_run: Create a docker-compose.yml with db (postgres:18), valkey (valkey/valkey:8-alpine), and pinepods services as shown in the README Quick Start
Set database and Valkey/Redis connection variables on the pinepods service
Open the server URL on port 8040 and create the first admin account
For an external Valkey/Redis server, set VALKEY_HOST and VALKEY_PORT and remove the local valkey service
stack: Flutter-style native apps (not named in README; omit)
notable: Central database keeps listening history, queue, and themes consistent across web, desktop, mobile, and CLI clients
Built-in gpodder-compatible sync server works alongside AntennaPod and similar apps
Multi-user with separate libraries, stats, and settings per user
Discovery across Podcast Index, iTunes, and YouTube, plus PodPeople DB host-following
Translated into 36 languages and ships multiple themes plus a custom theme creator
caveats: The API will not start if Valkey/Redis is unavailable, and Nginx then returns 502 for API requests
Upgrading an existing PostgreSQL 17 data directory to 18 requires a manual one-way upgrade with backup first
The public demo at try.pinepods.online is for evaluation only and is wiped periodically
